exposure_rules.title: No overnight cooling
exposure_rules.why: The outdoor temperature stays at or above 20 degrees overnight, so there is no window in which the home can cool down. The body recovers from daytime heat at night; without that recovery, each hot day compounds the one before it.

exposure_rules.title: Bedroom too hot to sleep safely
exposure_rules.why: The modelled overnight bedroom temperature is 26 degrees or above. Sleep is badly disrupted at this level and the strain on the heart continues through the night. This figure is modelled, not measured.

exposure_rules.title: Bedroom warmer than is restful
exposure_rules.why: The modelled overnight bedroom temperature is between 24 and 26 degrees. Sleep is disrupted above 24 degrees and the body does not fully recover from the day's heat. This figure is modelled, not measured.

exposure_rules.title: Peak feels-like temperature is high
exposure_rules.why: The apparent temperature reaches 30 degrees or above. Apparent temperature accounts for humidity, which is what determines whether sweating still cools the body.

exposure_rules.title: Third day or more of sustained heat
exposure_rules.why: Heat has been at or above the episode threshold for three consecutive days or more. Risk accumulates across a spell rather than resetting each morning, and the later days of an episode are the dangerous ones.

exposure_rules.title: Home below the healthy minimum
exposure_rules.why: The modelled daytime indoor temperature is between 16 and 18 degrees. Below 18 degrees, blood pressure rises and respiratory infections become more likely. This figure is modelled, not measured.

exposure_rules.title: Home cold enough to affect the heart and lungs
exposure_rules.why: The modelled daytime indoor temperature is between 12 and 16 degrees. Sustained exposure at this level raises the risk of heart attack and stroke. This figure is modelled, not measured.

exposure_rules.title: Home dangerously cold
exposure_rules.why: The modelled daytime indoor temperature is below 12 degrees. This is a serious risk to an older person, particularly overnight. This figure is modelled, not measured.

vulnerability_rules.title: Aged 85 or over
vulnerability_rules.why: Thermoregulation weakens with age, and thirst is felt less strongly. In summer 2025 this group had the highest heat-associated death rate in England at 364 per million.

vulnerability_rules.title: Aged 75 to 84
vulnerability_rules.why: Thermoregulation is measurably less effective in this age band, and the ability to compensate for heat or cold declines.

vulnerability_rules.title: Lives alone
vulnerability_rules.why: Nobody else is present to notice deterioration, encourage fluids, or call for help. Isolation converts a manageable problem into an unwitnessed one.

vulnerability_rules.title: Dementia
vulnerability_rules.why: Dementia can prevent someone recognising that they are too hot or too cold, or acting on it — removing layers, opening a window, or asking for a drink.

vulnerability_rules.title: Cardiovascular condition
vulnerability_rules.why: Heat raises heart rate and lowers blood pressure; cold raises blood pressure and thickens the blood. Both place additional load on a compromised heart.

vulnerability_rules.title: Kidney condition
vulnerability_rules.why: Impaired kidney function narrows the margin for fluid and electrolyte balance, which heat and sweating disturb directly.

vulnerability_rules.title: Respiratory condition
vulnerability_rules.why: Hot, humid or very cold air can each trigger breathing difficulty, and poor air quality often accompanies heat episodes.

vulnerability_rules.title: Limited mobility
vulnerability_rules.why: Reduced ability to move to a cooler or warmer room, adjust clothing, reach a drink, or leave the home for a cool space.

vulnerability_rules.title: Lithium and dehydration
vulnerability_rules.why: Dehydration raises lithium levels in the blood, and the safe range is narrow. Hot weather makes this more likely.

vulnerability_rules.title: Diuretic increases fluid and salt loss
vulnerability_rules.why: This medicine increases fluid and electrolyte loss, which compounds dehydration in hot weather.

vulnerability_rules.title: Medicine that reduces sweating
vulnerability_rules.why: This medicine can impair sweating, which is the body's main route for shedding heat.

vulnerability_rules.title: Medicine affecting temperature control
vulnerability_rules.why: This medicine can interfere with the brain's regulation of body temperature.

vulnerability_rules.title: Blood pressure medicine and fluid balance
vulnerability_rules.why: This class can blunt the sensation of thirst and adds strain on the kidneys when fluid is short.

vulnerability_rules.title: Beta blocker and skin blood flow
vulnerability_rules.why: This medicine reduces blood flow to the skin, which is one of the ways the body sheds heat.

vulnerability_rules.title: Antidepressant and sodium levels
vulnerability_rules.why: This class carries a risk of low blood sodium, which heat and heavy sweating can worsen.
